title: Waiting Until Diwali to Buy a Car? Check Official Dates Before You Delay
excerpt: Five launches are reportedly lined up for the festive window, but only Hyundai's Bayon has manufacturer documentation behind it — the rest lack official dates.
body:
• Media reports have linked five car launches to the Diwali 2026 buying window, but most carry no official launch date from the manufacturers.
  • The Hyundai Bayon is the exception: official manufacturer pages point to pricing and availability around Diwali 2026, giving it the only documented timeline.
  • The Tata Safari EV, Mahindra Thar facelift and Maruti Suzuki Fronx update are all widely reported yet officially unconfirmed — buyers should check company documentation before delaying a purchase.
  • Diwali remains India's peak car-buying season, which is exactly why unverified launch rumours carry the most weight now.

Thinking of holding off on a car purchase until Diwali? Business Today has flagged a problem with that plan: of the five launches reportedly lined up for the festive window, not all have official dates — and some may not arrive on the rumoured schedule at all.

The festive season is India's peak car-buying period, when manufacturers time launches to catch the wave of auspicious purchases. That dynamic creates fertile ground for rumour: a widely repeated launch window can feel like a confirmed date even when the manufacturer has said nothing. The reporting cautions buyers to check official documentation before delaying a purchase on the strength of a media report.

The one with a paper trail: Hyundai Bayon

The Hyundai Bayon stands apart. Official manufacturer pages indicate that pricing and availability are expected around Diwali 2026, according to LatestLY — making it one of the few vehicles on the rumour list with tangible corporate documentation behind it. For buyers cross-shopping compact SUVs, the Bayon is the launch they can most plausibly plan around.

The reported but unconfirmed: Safari EV, Thar facelift, Fronx update

The Tata Safari EV is heavily linked to the festive window in reports, with industry chatter pointing to a flagship seven-seater electric SUV offering 600–627 km of claimed range. But Tata.ev's official documentation currently omits the model entirely, even as the company actively markets the Harrier.ev. The exact launch timeline remains unconfirmed by official channels.

Mahindra's Thar facelift is similarly reported — revised exterior styling and upgraded cabin technology, per industry sources — but Mahindra's current digital catalogue shows only standard variants of the three-door off-roader, with no acknowledgement of a facelift schedule. And the Maruti Suzuki Fronx update, widely discussed for a revised front fascia and modified petrol engine configuration, has no dated confirmation in Maruti Suzuki's official releases. The timeline sits strictly in the projected category.

Why the caution matters now

The advice is practical, not cynical. Delaying a purchase for a launch that slips — or never materialises on the rumoured date — can cost buyers in two ways: festive-season offers and financing deals on current models expire, and waiting buyers lose months of use. Manufacturers, for their part, have every incentive to stay vague: confirming a date too early freezes showroom traffic, while denying one kills the buzz.

The pattern is familiar to anyone who follows the Indian auto market. Tata is simultaneously working on a broader EV push — the Sierra EV, an Avinya-based premium EV and next-generation mass-market electric models — which gives the company plenty of launch levers to pull, but also plenty of reason to keep the Safari EV's timing fluid.

What's next

Diwali falls in early November this year, so the window for official announcements is now. Watch for manufacturer press releases and brochure updates — particularly from Tata and Mahindra — in the coming weeks. Until then, treat reported launch windows as what they are: reports. If the car you need is in showrooms today with a festive offer attached, the bird in hand may be the better buy.
